- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.16) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a recent price spike (e.g., >83), model often overshoots downward in next 5–10 days — cap forecast decline to 1–2% below peak or align with 3–5 day moving average.
- If sentiment shows strong positive spikes (e.g., >0.61) followed by negative, model often fails to revert — force mean reversion toward 10–15 day average or add 0.5–1.0 point downward adjustment.
- Model consistently overestimates short-term (1–3 day) downward moves when sentiment is negative — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 point for next 3 days if sentiment < -0.16.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early decline (first 5–7 days) — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5 points if sentiment is negative or volatile.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overestimate downward trend — add 0.5–1.0 point upward bias to first 5 days of forecast.
